segments.text: This is Tony C. from The Shoes.
You were building casseroles in the sand.
I brought a fork, you brought a marching band.
You buttered me up just to toast me brown.
Then crossed my name off the lost and found.
You drew me out of your coloring book.
I lost my place when the radiator shook
There was something important I meant to accuse
But the words fell out through a hole in my shoes
You turned me to scones
And the scones don't need you
My beautiful reducer
My beautiful Medusa
I'm losing the remote, don't even care
Somebody left all the snakes downstairs
You turned me to scones
Now the kettle's coming home
When first I met you, you were wearing a raincoat
I called it a halo, that's what my brain wrote
Now I realize underneath that sleeve
You had 17 receipts and a wheel of cheese
You said forever, I heard four leather chairs
I carried them up 17 flights of stairs
You gave me a look that could petrify bread
I thanked the conductor and climbed into bed
You turned me to scones
And the scones don't need you
My beautiful Reducer
My beautiful Medusa
I'm losing the remote, don't even care
Somebody left all the snakes downstairs
You turned me to scones
Now the kettle's coming home
Surprised every morning my socks aren't dead
Got a mouthful of coupons and cabbage for a head
Check the mirror, both thighs were plaid
That's the finest reflection, not almost
The bottle said shampoo, the sandwich said leave
I wiped all my prophecies off of my sleeve
There's a crop of last verse somewhere under this chair
But a pigeon has eaten it fair is fair
You turned me to scones
But I finally forgive you, my beautiful Reducin', my beautiful Medusa
Lost every word, found you sittin' there With a little crooked smile and a snake in your hair
I'll put down the page, let the kitchen light glow My beautiful Medusa, that's the one I know
Surprised every morning my song
